transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

People at work are plotting against me and changing my routes on purpose, and no one believes me when I tell them it’s happening. My husband and my boss just brush it off as stress or computer glitches, but I know someone is actively doing this to make me look incompetent.
How long have you been experiencing these concerns about people at work, and have you had any other unusual experiences or changes in your behavior during this time?

The plotting has been really bad for the last couple of months, though I've felt things slipping for about a year. I've also started freezing at my desk or pacing and muttering under my breath, and I've stopped caring about choir, softball, or even talking to my husband. Most days I just lie on the couch in my uniform because everything feels like too much effort.

Have you noticed any times where you felt like you were hearing voices or seeing things that others could not, and how long exactly have these specific concerns about people plotting against you been the primary focus of your life?

No, I haven't heard any voices or seen anything unusual like that. The intense feeling that people are plotting against me and changing my routes has really taken over as my main focus for the last couple of months, though it started as a nagging suspicion over the past year.

Besides the suspicion about your coworkers, have you noticed a significant decline in your ability to speak fluidly or express emotions, such as your face appearing 'flat' or your speech becoming very limited?

Yes, I feel completely empty inside and don't really show any emotion anymore. It takes so much effort to speak that I usually just give my husband one-word answers when he tries to talk to me. I've just stopped caring about everything.
Have you noticed that your ability to perform your job duties or manage your daily hygiene has significantly declined over the past year, beyond just the feelings of suspicion?

Yes, it's gotten really bad over the last year, and I'm actually on a final warning at work now because of the mistakes. At home, I don't even have the energy to shower, cook, or help with chores anymore. Most days I just lie on the couch in my work uniform because doing anything at all feels like too much effort.
Have you noticed that your speech has become incoherent or that you have begun to act in ways that seem bizarre or purposeless to others, such as sudden, odd movements or strange facial expressions?

Yes, I've had moments where I just freeze at my desk, staring at the screen or holding the phone without answering it. Other times, I pace up and down the hallway muttering about the routes under my breath. I know people are watching me weirdly, but I just can't seem to make myself act normal in those moments.

During those times when you freeze or pace, do you feel like you are unable to move or speak even when you want to, or is it more that your thoughts feel jumbled and your actions feel disorganized or unpredictable?

It feels more like my thoughts are completely jumbled and I just can't force myself to act normal. When I freeze at my desk or pace the hallways muttering about the routes, I know people are staring at me, but I can't make myself stop. It's like my mind and my actions are totally disconnected in those moments and I just can't behave the way I'm supposed to.

When you freeze at your desk, do you ever find yourself holding a fixed, unusual position for a long period, or do you find that your behaviors are primarily characterized by disorganized, purposeless movements?

I don't think I hold strange positions, but I do just freeze up and stare at the screen or hold the phone without answering it. It's more that I get stuck pacing the hallway and muttering the routes under my breath, and I just can't force myself to act normally during those times.
When you freeze or pace, do you ever find that you are completely unresponsive to people around you, or do you remain aware of what is happening even though you feel unable to control your body?

I definitely remain aware of everything going on around me during those times. I can see people watching me weirdly and hear the phone ringing, but I just feel completely stuck. I'm conscious of it all, I just can't make myself respond or control my actions in the moment.

When you have these episodes of freezing or pacing, is your behavior primarily disorganized and unpredictable, or is it more of a persistent, fixed belief that the people around you are part of a specific, structured conspiracy against you?

The freezing and pacing happen because I feel like I've lost control and can't make myself act normal in the moment. It is really driven by how overwhelmed and consumed I am by the constant, certain belief that my coworkers are actively plotting and sabotaging my routes behind my back. That knowledge is always there, and it just completely takes over my mind.
